- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates upside; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to capture momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price increases when sentiment turns bullish; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days of forecast.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight upward bias to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome by 1–3% over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion correction: add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days if sentiment remains neutral or slightly bullish.
